title: tool-annotations-stable-choice-serialization-and-fragment-safe-streaming
author: Maya Ortega
description: Context: Customers reported rare nondeterministic tool selection during streamed OpenAI-compatible responses where the model returned multiple candidate tool choices split across streaming fragments. This caused downstream systems to sometimes pick different tools after reassembly. Motivation: make the OpenAI adapter produce deterministic, replay-safe tool_choice selection and deliver tool payloads with fragment-safe markers so reassembly cannot change choice. What this PR does: 1) Introduces a canonical serialization path for tool choice and tool descriptors: ToolDescriptor v2 with canonical field ordering and stable hashing. This prevents dict-order nondeterminism when computing tool signatures used by routable policies. 2) Adds lightweight per-chunk framing markers in the streaming envelope to ensure the boundary between a tool_choice event and its associated tool payload cannot be split by arbitrary chunking. The runtime now inserts an explicit "chunk_boundary_hint" token in the stream for cases where a tool_choice is immediately followed by a tool payload. 3) Augments the adapter mapping rules so vendor tool schemas (OpenAPI-like or freeform) are normalized into ToolDescriptor v2, including explicit parameter typing and a normalized examples array. 4) Implements deterministic tie-breaking heuristics for tool_choice when the model returns multiple candidates with equal score: prefer higher-explicit-priority annotation, then lexicographic tool-id, then stable-hash of canonical descriptor. 5) Adds compatibility layer to avoid changing external OpenAI-compatible JSON for customers relying on legacy frames: the adapter emits the new markers only when client indicates support via the X-Redwood-OpenAI-Compat header. 6) Tests + benchmarks: unit tests for serialization round-trip, end-to-end streaming tests that simulate fragment boundaries, and a lightweight perf benchmark demonstrating ~1% median token-latency regression on small cases but eliminating nondeterministic reassembly failures. Checklist: - [x] Spec: include canonicalization rules and framing E2E contract - [x] Implementation: adapter + runtime framing + policy tie-breaker - [x] Tests: serializer unit tests, streaming e2e harness, and regression alerts - [x] Docs: SDK typings update and migration notes - [x] Rollout plan: feature-flagged by default off, opt-in via header; staged rollout to dedicated customers Impact/risk: low functional change (opt-in), but careful rollout required for clients that parse raw stream fragments. Related: ENG-4871 (deterministic routing), ENG-4920 (stream reassembly incidents), SUP-1221 (support ticket about changing tool in flight).
commits: feat(adapter): add ToolDescriptor v2 + canonical serializer
feat(runtime): insert chunk_boundary_hint for tool payload transition
chore(tests): add streaming reassembly harness and unit tests
perf: add benchmark measuring token latency of additional framing markers
docs: add migration note and SDK typedefs for ToolDescriptor v2
review_conversation:
Ivy Chen: Can you clarify why we need canonical JSON vs. protobuf? The team is concerned about adding yet another schema.
Maya Ortega: We considered protobuf but the OpenAI surface expects JSON and many clients reserialize; canonical JSON lets us interoperate without changing external shapes and avoids introducing a new wire format.

Lars Müller: The chunk_boundary_hint looks fine but will it increase stream size noticeably?
Maya Ortega: It adds a very small token in the stream only for boundary cases; benchmark shows <1% median token latency impact and negligible bandwidth increase on typical traffic.

Priya Natarajan: We should gate this behind the compat header for the first rollout to avoid surprising customers.
Maya Ortega: Agreed. Default behavior remains unchanged; header opt-in flips the adapter to emit framing markers and canonical descriptors.

Ivy Chen: Please add a real-world test using the mobile client chunker; it's been flaky before.
Maya Ortega: Added a mobile chunker simulation in the integration harness and ran it against two deduped agent scenarios; results included in CI.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in OpenAI adapter feature that emits canonical tool descriptors and fragment-safe streaming markers to eliminate nondeterministic tool selection during fragmented streaming. Backwards-compatible and gated by X-Redwood-OpenAI-Compat header.
notes_for_releasers: Feature is off by default. To enable for a customer, flip runtime feature flag 'openai_adapter.canonical_tool_choice' and instruct client to set X-Redwood-OpenAI-Compat: v2. Monitor streaming_reassembly_failures alert for first 48h.
migration_steps: 1) Clients that parse raw framed fragments must opt-in after testing; 2) SDKs updated with ToolDescriptor v2 typedefs; 3) Operators can enable feature-flag per-customer in Console; 4) If issues, revert by disabling header or rolling back feature flag.
notes: This PR intentionally minimizes surface area change by keeping external JSON stable unless the compat header is present. It centralizes tool normalization logic to make future policy work easier.
